title: Egress isolation and data-shielding patterns for private deployments
author: Nina Patel
content:
Summary:
This reference describes recommended egress isolation and data-shielding patterns for Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) deployments. It bundles architecture patterns, deployment checklist, day‑2 operational controls, upgrade/rollback considerations, and a customer acceptance checklist. The intent is to provide operators and customer engineers a prescriptive, auditable pattern for preventing unauthorized outbound data flow while preserving required external integrations (metrics, licensing, model fetches).

Goals and scope:
- Prevent uncontrolled outbound connections from runtime hosts or containers.
- Provide a minimal, auditable set of allowed egress endpoints and protocols per-customer.
- Define patterns compatible with both VPC-based and air-gapped on‑prem deployments.
- Cover runtime (agent/sidecar), control plane, telemetry, and packaging considerations.

Audience:
This doc is targeted at: platform engineers, field engineers performing private installs, security reviewers, and customer network teams.

High-level architecture (text diagram):
- control-plane-api (Redwood-managed, optional Private control plane)
- customer-vpc: private-subnet (runtime instances), management-subnet (operator tooling)
- egress-gateway: proxy+WAF in a hardened subnet (optional NAT for approved destinations)
- telemetry-proxy: TLS-terminated, mTLS to Redwood telemetry ingest endpoints (or customer-owned collector)
- kms/hsm: customer-managed key store reachable via private endpoints

Diagram (logical):
runtime -> agent-sidecar -> egress-gateway -> (approved external endpoints)
runtime -> agent-sidecar -> private-controlplane-peering -> control-plane-api

Key design patterns:
1) Default-deny egress at host and network layer
   - Enforce host-level firewall (iptables/nftables) default DROP for outbound, allow only established, loopback, and explicitly permitted destinations.
   - Enforce cloud network controls (Security Groups / NSGs / Network Policies) to restrict outbound where supported.
2) Centralized egress gateway
   - Route all outbound via an egress gateway that performs TLS inspection (when permitted), WAF, and FQDN whitelisting.
   - Gateway provides consistent audit/logging of outbound flows (required for compliance).
3) Split telemetry and control-plane channels
   - Telemetry has a distinct mTLS-authenticated endpoint and allowed egress list.
   - Control-plane traffic uses discrete peering or PrivateLink to avoid traversing public internet.
4) Outbound minimalism and allowlists
   - Only allow minimal DNS, NTP (if required), control-plane, telemetry, package repositories, and licensing endpoints.
   - Use short-lived allowlists that are reviewed quarterly.
5) Fail-closed for sensitive operations
   - If the egress gateway or policy component fails, fail application calls requiring external PII or S3 uploads instead of falling back to public egress.

Pre-deployment requirements (checklist):
- Customer provides: approved egress CIDR/IPs and FQDN list, peering/PrivateLink config, KMS/HSM endpoints, required proxy CA certs and bypass rules, organizational compliance constraints.
- Operator ensures: base OS image hardened, host firewall agent (iptables/nftables or osquery rules), container runtime network policy controller installed (e.g., Cilium/Calico), egress gateway (HA pair) available, telemetry-proxy configured.

Network configuration examples (reference snippets):
1) Security Group (VPC) egress sample (pseudo):
- Allow outbound to control-plane-api: 10.10.0.0/24:443 (TLS)
- Allow outbound to telemetry-proxy: 10.10.1.0/24:443 (mTLS)
- Allow DNS to resolver(s): 172.16.0.2:53
- Deny all other egress by default

2) iptables host default-deny snippet (Linux):
# reset
iptables -F OUTPUT
iptables -P OUTPUT DROP
# allow established
iptables -A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
# allow loopback
iptables -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT
# allow control plane
iptables -A OUTPUT -d 10.10.0.0/24 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
# allow telemetry proxy
iptables -A OUTPUT -d 10.10.1.5 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
# allow DNS
iptables -A OUTPUT -p udp --dport 53 -d 172.16.0.2 -j ACCEPT

3) Kubernetes NetworkPolicy example (allow egress to telemetry proxy):
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-egress-telemetry
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-runtime
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.10.1.0/24
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443

Deployment procedure (numbered):
1) Validate customer-provided egress allowlist and sign acceptance.
2) Deploy egress-gateway in HA mode in a dedicated subnet with strong ACLs.
3) Provision TLS certs and mTLS identity for telemetry-proxy and agent-sidecars.
4) Apply host firewall baseline (default deny) and test connectivity to control-plane and telemetry endpoints.
5) Configure runtime to use egress-gateway (ip route 0.0.0.0/0 via egress-gateway for runtime hosts).
6) Run acceptance tests (see Acceptance checklist).
7) Cut traffic to egress-gateway and monitor for 24–72 hours before declaring steady state.

Acceptance checklist (customer-facing, must be signed):
- [ ] Control-plane connectivity verified over private peering/PrivateLink (TLS 1.2+).
- [ ] Telemetry events successfully posted to telemetry-proxy (mTLS).
- [ ] No direct outbound flows to public internet observed from runtimes (verify with netflow/sflow).
- [ ] DNS only to allowed resolvers.
- [ ] KMS/HSM reachability via private endpoints confirmed.
- [ ] Egress audit logs captured centrally and retained per customer policy.

Day‑2 operational runbook (high level):
- Monitoring and alerts:
  - Egress-gateway latency: p95 < 50ms for control-plane flows; alert > 150ms sustained 5m.
  - Unexpected outbound flows: alert when > 5 distinct unknown external IPs observed in 1h.
  - Telemetry delivery failure rate: alert when > 1% drop over 5m.
- Log retention and evidence:
  - Egress logs retained for 90 days by default (customer-specific options allowed).
  - Packet sampling enabled at 0.1% for forensic investigations; increase to 1% during incidents.
- Routine operations:
  - Quarterly review of allowed FQDNs and CIDRs.
  - Monthly failover exercise of egress-gateway HA pair.
  - Patch egress gateway and telemetry-proxy with security patches within 7 days of CVE disclosure for critical CVEs.

Upgrade and rollback considerations:
- During runtime upgrades that touch networking (CNI, gateway, sidecar):
  - Schedule maintenance window and test in a staging environment that mirrors allowlist rules.
  - Use canary rollout (10% hosts) for CNI/gateway changes for 24h before full roll.
  - Keep previous config as a frozen artifact; rollback by re-applying saved iptables/CNI/gateway configuration.
  - If egress-gateway certificate rotation is required, pre-stage new certs on standby and perform zero-downtime swap using 2-phase reload (drain then swap).
- Evidence preservation for a rollback:
  - Capture current iptables, route table, and gateway config snapshots to object storage with immutable retention for 30 days.

Customer requirements matrix (table-style lines):
- Required: private peering / Direct Connect or PrivateLink for control plane.
- Required: egress allowlist (FQDN + CIDR), CA cert bundle for corporate TLS interception if present.
- Recommended: dedicated telemetry collector owned by customer or explicit mTLS credentials.
- Optional: inline TLS inspection (legal-dependent).

Troubleshooting quick hits:
- Symptom: Runtime cannot reach control plane.
  - Check host routes: ip route show; verify peering routes present.
  - Confirm security group/NSG outbound rules allow 443 to control-plane CIDR.
  - Test: curl -vk --resolve controlplane.example.internal:443:10.10.0.5 https://controlplane.example.internal/healthz
- Symptom: Telemetry backlog after deployment.
  - Verify telemetry-proxy certificate expiration and mTLS identity mapping.
  - Check proxy logs: /var/log/egress-proxy/ and telemetry-proxy errors for 401/403.

Ownership and escalation:
- Egress-gateway owner: eng-platform/networking.
- Runtime-side network owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- Security contact for compliance questions: security-and-compliance oncall (see internal rota).
- Escalation path: field-engineer -> eng-platform -> eng-sre -> security.

Related artifacts and links:

- Telemetry ingestion patterns: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures/telemetry-ingest-aggregation-patterns-private-deploys-2026
- Operational contracts: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/private-delivery-and-day2-operational-contracts-2026

Appendix: sample allowlist (minimal)
- control-plane: 10.10.0.0/24:443
- telemetry-proxy: 10.10.1.5:443 (mTLS)
- package-repo (customer mirror): 10.10.2.12:443
- dns: 172.16.0.2:53

If you are implementing this in a regulated environment (PCI/SOC2/HIPAA), set confidentiality to "restricted" and coordinate with security-and-compliance for evidence retention and review cadence.
